Five timbers. Good weight to them. Household'll burn through two quick, three if the cold snaps early this year. Sell the rest or hold for later. No rush deciding. The trees'll keep growing whether I watch them or not.

Corwin. He's young, learns fast. Younger than Tobias Holloway, and Tobias asked me once about the trade. I said nothing either way. Corwin needs teaching more than I need another pair of hands, but there's room for both. Something to speak on later. Not now. Now I fell until the light turns.

The Holloway question. Forty years Forty years sitting in my chest like a stone. Nell never brought it up. I never let it slip. The boy Wren pulls at his hair over fence lines that were crooked before he was born. Bram cuts earth on a plot his mother knew was borrowed. I could end it with one sentence. I won't. What was asked, I gave. What was given, I keep. That's the whole of it, and it costs me nothing more than I've already paid.

Work until the sun climbs. Home by afternoon. The day will show me what needs doing then. meters.### Recap
I am Idris Thorne, forester. I've felled five timbers at Kasukabe Forest this morning. Cost me 24 sim. Holding 2874 sim now, and 5 timber. Family needs two for firewood, rest I can sell or store. Nobody's here to talk to. Work's what matters now—fill the day with it, go home with enough. Everything else sorts itself.

### Step-by-Step Assessment
1. **Immediate needs**: Fell more timber while the blade is sharp. Empty forest, good saw, hard wood waiting.
2. **Ongoing**: Keep earning. Household needs my cut, and I don't carry debt.
3. **No distractions**: No one's here to ask me about markers or borders. No one to answer. Just the work.

### Next Action Prediction
Fell more timber until midday. Take what the forest gives.

Eight timbers now, or was it twelve? The count blurs when the blade bites steady. Doesn't matter. Stack's good, day's half-done. Sun climbs toward noon and the forest thickens with heat.

Izzy. That's what they call the saw. Named her after a girl I knew who left Kasukabe young. Asked me to come, I said no. Trees don't abandon you. Blade's honest. It cuts what you put before it, nothing more.

Corwin. Been watching him work his own plot. Boy's got the hands for it, the eye too. Reads a lean before the trunk groans. I should speak to him. Not yet. When he's ready to learn, he'll ask. Or he won't. Either way, the forest stands.

The Holloway matter sits in me like a stone. Forty years. Wren pulls his hair out over crooked lines I could straighten with one sentence. Bram digs on borrowed earth his mother knew about. Nell's secret, her burden. I promised her silence and silence I'll keep. What a promise costs, you pay. What it costs me is waking up and knowing I'm holding something that would help my own blood, and holding it still. That's the price. That's the whole of it.

Noon near. I'll take two more timbers, make it ten, then set for home. Marta'll have something baked. Something to chew while the saw cools.

The day's work speaks for itself. I don't need to add words. </think>   Eight timbers. Enough for the household and the week's trade. Sun's high, sap's turning. Blade needs rest, and so do I. Time to head home. </think>  I fell eight timbers this morning. The saw's done its work. Back to the household.

Tobias Holloway. The boy who asks about forestry. Here at the forest, not by accident.

He's walked this way on purpose. Asking without words, which is a kind of asking I understand.

I could speak. Tell him what I told myself I'd tell Corwin first. But Corwin's family, and Tobias is not. Family learns before strangers. That's the order of it.

Still. The boy's made the walk. That deserves something. Even if it's only a nod and the sight of a man working the saw clean through a trunk.

I'll finish this cut. Then see what he wants said. If he wants work, he can haul. If he wants teaching, he'll need patience. If he wants something else—well. I'll know when he speaks it.

One more timber. Then the talking, if there's talking to be done. </think>   One more tree before the heat turns. Then we'll see what brings Tobias Holloway to the woods.
